short_answer: Joe D'Amico is a real, active, long running Las Vegas handicapper. He has written NFL betting breakdowns for the Las Vegas Review-Journal as recently as December 2024, entered its handicapper contests for years, and posts picks almost daily. His picks are on sale today on StatSalt and Winners and Whiners, both run by Wager Talk Media, LP, and on the SportsCapping network. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money over time is a separate question. Every record on his sales pages is a streak or a short window chosen by the seller. The one long, independent record we could open is the Review-Journal contest, where his entries we found ran from 27-28-1 to 35-30, close to break even against the spread.

Treat him as a well known name with marketing records, not a proven long term winner. The same kind of pass costs noticeably more on one network than the other, so compare before you pay, and record every pick yourself.

guarantee: On the SportsCapping network, the Capper Reviews guarantee policy says handicappers guarantee packages so "you either profit or else you will be compensated with a subscription of equal time free of charge" and that "We do not offer a money back policy." The limits are strict: no free time if the package made any profit at all, plays graded on "100 unit intervals", only one free period per purchase even if that also loses, grading on the odds the handicapper chose, and "There is NO GUARANTEE on seasonal subscriptions." His 30 day package copy on Vegas Top Dogs says "We guarantee you'll make a profit or we'll give you 30 more days at NO EXTRA COST!" and his 90 day blurb on Capper Reviews says "PROFIT IS GUARANTEED!" Under the policy, that means more picks, not money.

On StatSalt and Winners and Whiners, daily picks also come in a higher priced guaranteed version, but the pages we opened did not explain what that guarantee pays. The Winners and Whiners refund policy says "All Sales are Final" and that once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed "no refunds will be issued." Its FAQ says "No picks or predictions are guaranteed." Nothing on either network covers losses on the bets themselves, which are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: We checked the badges against the latest 20 picks StatSalt lists for him, graded by the same network. For games played from 7 Nov 2026 the list shows 13 wins and 4 losses, not 13 and 2. The badge leaves out the two college basketball losses on 13 Nov. Winners and Whiners showed "+30.35%" for the same window while StatSalt showed "+25.55%".

The "9-2 NCAAF RUN" headline did not match the list either. The ten picks labeled NCAAF in his latest 20 went 7 wins and 3 losses. The list may not include every pick, so we report the gap without drawing more from it.

On the SportsCapping network, the 3 day and 180 day package blurbs read "4-7 this season" without naming a sport, while the same page advertises "13-3 (81.3%)" since 7 Nov. Short windows like these change daily and every start date is chosen by the seller.

We did not find Review-Journal pages for the 2007 or 2010 contest results, so those wins remain his claim. The contest pages we could open show him as an entrant with ordinary records, covered under the record section below.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: three Las Vegas Review-Journal contest snapshots we opened. On 24 Sep 2011 his college challenge record was 7-7. On 6 Dec 2014 his NFL challenge record was 35-30, about 54%. On 28 Nov 2015 it was 27-28-1. These are five or so picks a week against the spread, not his paid plays, but they are kept by a newspaper, not by a seller.

What the seller publishes: StatSalt lists his latest 20 graded picks, dated 5 Nov to 13 Nov 2026. We counted 14 wins and 6 losses (70%). At one unit per pick at the listed odds that is about +5.6 units; weighted by his 3 and 4 star ratings it is about +19 units on 74 risked. Fourteen of the 20 were football. This is a hot nine days, graded by the network that sells the picks.
We found no full, time stamped log of every pick he has sold, no court or regulator record about him, and no third party audit.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence about Joe D'Amico is thin. Most comments sit on a review site that belongs to one of the networks selling his picks.

customers.text: We found very little independent comment on Joe D'Amico from buyers. On Covers in October 2023, a member who advises against buying picks ranked him among the worst handicappers promoted on websites and YouTube, saying he talks a lot and tries to sell everything. Capper Reviews, a site in the SportsCapping network that sells his picks, shows a 4.02 out of 5 rating from 58 votes and 11 undated comments: one says every time they bought his picks they lost, several praise winning runs, and others talk about his morning show. CapperTek lists no reviews for AASIWins.com. Our library of buyer posts had no paid buyer story about him. We found no complaint about billing or refunds and no regulator action. Our Reddit search was partial. The Reddit archive's full text search timed out on 17 Nov 2026, so we checked our saved copy of ten betting subreddits and a few title searches instead; none mentioned him.

A Covers member listed five least favorite handicappers promoted on websites and YouTube and put him third, saying he talks a lot, tries to sell everything, and that his picks are bad. The poster did not say they had bought any picks, and gave no record.

One commenter on his Capper Reviews page wrote that he is "all talk" and that every time they bought his picks, the picks lost. No dates or amounts are given. The site is part of the network that sells his packages.

Several commenters on the same page praise him: one credits an 11 of 14 run on NFL picks over about a year, others cite a Monday night winner and a hot run in MLB. None shows a receipt or record, and the comments sit on a site that sells his picks.
Other comments on the page are about his personality and a morning show, which two commenters said they enjoyed or want back. They say nothing about whether the picks win.
CapperTek's page for AASIWins.com, his longtime site, listed no reviews or complaints.
Web searches of Covers, Sportsbook Review, TheRX and general results found no buyer complaint, refund dispute or results thread about his paid picks beyond the Covers post above.

conflicts: StatSalt and Winners and Whiners grade his picks, show his badges and sell his packages; Winners and Whiners says its sales are made by Wager Talk Media, LP. Capper Reviews says plainly that it is part of the SportsCapping network that sells his picks. The ratings and comments on that page come from the seller's side of the deal.

StatSalt and Winners and Whiners say they may receive a commission if you open an account through a bookmaker or casino link on their sites. That proves nothing about his picks, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.
strengths: A real, public figure with a long media history: the Review-Journal has run his picks and NFL breakdowns from 2011 to at least 2024.
Every package on both networks has a published price, and single picks start at $25.00.
StatSalt shows a list of his latest 20 graded picks with the odds, star rating and sportsbook, losses included.
He has entered public contests where his record is kept by a newspaper, which many pick sellers never do.
The SportsCapping network guarantee gives a free repeat period on short packages that lose.
concerns: No full public record. Every number on his sales pages is a streak or a short window chosen by the seller.
Badges and headlines did not match his own pick list on the day we checked (13-2 shown, 13-4 listed; a 9-2 college football run shown, 7-3 in the list).
The independent contest records we found were close to break even: 7-7, 35-30 and 27-28-1.
The same kind of pass costs more on one network than the other, for example $69 for 3 days on StatSalt and $99.00 on the SportsCapping network.
Guarantees pay in more picks, never cash, and not at all on season passes. Winners and Whiners says all sales are final.
Big bio claims, such as casino managers trembling and contest wins in 2007 and 2010, are not backed by anything we could open.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Compare the price of the same pass on StatSalt, Winners and Whiners and the SportsCapping sites before you buy.
Count units, not wins. Several of his recent picks were money line favorites at -134 to -170, which need a high win rate to profit.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and free days. Here a losing package earns more picks, and season passes get nothing.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
faq: He is a real, long running Las Vegas handicapper whose picks are sold by two established pick networks with written terms, and the Review-Journal has published his picks for years. We found no court or regulator action involving him. Whether his picks win over the long run is not shown by anything we could open.
How much does Joe D'Amico cost?

On 17 Nov 2026, single picks ran $25.00 to $39.00. StatSalt sold all sports passes at $39 for 1 day, $69 for 3 days, $99 for 7 days and $299 for 30 days. The SportsCapping network charged $49.95 to $1,999.95 for 1 to 365 days, and $120.00 to $899.99 for season packages.
Does Joe D'Amico have a verified record?

No full one. His latest 20 picks on StatSalt went 14 and 6, graded by the seller's own network. The independent contest records we found were 7-7 in 2011 college picks, 35-30 in 2014 NFL picks and 27-28-1 in 2015 NFL picks.
Does Joe D'Amico offer a refund?

No cash refunds. On the SportsCapping network a losing short package earns one free repeat period, with no guarantee on season passes. Winners and Whiners says all sales are final and no picks are guaranteed.

On StatSalt and Winners and Whiners (Wager Talk Media, LP, Las Vegas) and on SportsCapping network sites such as Capper Reviews and Vegas Top Dogs. His old site, AASIWins.com, still loads but shows a 2010 footer.

For $25 you get one daily pick with marketing built on short hot runs. What is unproven is whether his paid picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over a long stretch, and his public contest records sat near that line. Nothing refunds your betting losses.
